generic: Live Attenuated Varicella-Zoster Virus Vaccine (Oka/Merck strain)
pharm: Active immunizing agent (varicella and herpes zoster prophylaxis)
quick: Varicella (VARIVAX): 0.5 mL SC x2 doses 4-8 wks apart; Zoster (ZOSTAVAX): 0.65 mL SC single dose
Contraindicated; avoid pregnancy for 1-3 months after vaccination
Use with caution; benefit generally outweighs theoretical risk
summary: Live attenuated varicella-zoster virus vaccine uses the Oka/Merck strain to induce protective immunity against VZV disease. Two distinct live products share this strain: VARIVAX, given subcutaneously as a 2-dose series to children 12 months and older and to susceptible adolescents and adults for prevention of varicella (chickenpox); and ZOSTAVAX, a higher-potency single subcutaneous dose formerly used in adults 50-60 years and older to prevent herpes zoster (shingles) and postherpetic neuralgia. As a live vaccine, the entire class is contraindicated in significant immunosuppression and in pregnancy. ZOSTAVAX was discontinued in the US market in 2020 and has been replaced by the non-live recombinant zoster vaccine (Shingrix); VARIVAX remains the standard live varicella vaccine.
indications: VARIVAX: active immunization for the prevention of varicella (chickenpox) in individuals 12 months of age and older
ZOSTAVAX (now discontinued in the US): prevention of herpes zoster (shingles) in adults 50 years and older (routinely used from age 60)
ZOSTAVAX historically reduced the incidence and severity of postherpetic neuralgia

dosage.c: Varicella prevention - children 12 months to 12 years (VARIVAX)
dosage.n: 1st at 12-15 months, 2nd at 4-6 years (minimum 3 months apart)

dosage.c: Varicella prevention - adolescents and adults >=13 years (VARIVAX)
dosage.n: Doses 4 to 8 weeks apart for susceptible individuals
Higher virus titer than VARIVAX; discontinued in the US since 2020 - recombinant zoster vaccine now preferred

admin: Administer subcutaneously, preferably in the outer aspect of the upper arm (deltoid) or anterolateral thigh
Reconstitute only with the supplied diluent immediately before use and inject promptly (within 30 minutes)
Do not inject intravascularly or intramuscularly
Use a separate syringe and do not mix with any other vaccine in the same syringe
Maintain the cold chain; the lyophilized vaccine requires frozen storage and protection from light
Discard reconstituted vaccine if not used within the labeled time window
moa: The vaccine contains live, attenuated varicella-zoster virus (Oka/Merck strain). Subcutaneous administration produces a controlled subclinical infection that stimulates humoral (anti-VZV antibody) and cell-mediated immune responses and generates immunologic memory. For varicella prevention (VARIVAX), this primed immunity prevents or attenuates chickenpox on subsequent natural exposure. For zoster prevention (ZOSTAVAX), the higher-titer dose boosts waning VZV-specific cell-mediated immunity in older adults, reducing reactivation of latent virus that causes shingles.

absolute: History of anaphylactic/anaphylactoid reaction to the vaccine, gelatin, or neomycin
Primary or acquired immunodeficiency (e.g., advanced symptomatic HIV, leukemia, lymphoma, blood dyscrasias)
Immunosuppressive therapy (including high-dose corticosteroids, biologics, chemotherapy)
relative: Recent receipt of immune globulin or blood products (defer vaccination by the appropriate interval)
Family history of congenital/hereditary immunodeficiency until immune competence is established
Concurrent salicylate (aspirin) therapy in children - avoid for 6 weeks after varicella vaccination
Concurrent antivirals active against herpesviruses (acyclovir, valacyclovir, famciclovir) - may reduce vaccine effectiveness
monitor: Avoidance of contact with high-risk susceptible individuals if a rash develops

preg: Contraindicated in pregnancy. Effects on fetal development are unknown and the live vaccine virus poses a theoretical risk. Do not vaccinate pregnant women. Advise avoiding pregnancy for at least 1 month, and per some guidance up to 3 months, after vaccination.
lact: It is not known whether vaccine virus is excreted in human milk; wild-type VZV is not known to be transmitted via breast milk. Use with caution in breastfeeding women - the benefit of maternal immunity generally outweighs the theoretical risk.
renal: No dose adjustment is required for renal impairment.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is required for hepatic impairment.

major: Immunosuppressants / high-dose corticosteroids / chemotherapy / biologics (impaired response and risk of disseminated vaccine-strain infection - contraindicated)
Immune globulin / whole blood / plasma products (may blunt the immune response - separate administration by the recommended interval)
moderate: Antivirals active against herpesviruses (acyclovir, valacyclovir, famciclovir) - may inactivate the live vaccine virus; avoid 24 hours before through 14 days after vaccination
Salicylates / aspirin in children (avoid for 6 weeks after varicella vaccination due to reported Reye syndrome association)
Other live vaccines (administer on the same day or separate by at least 4 weeks)
interactions.diagnostics: May transiently suppress tuberculin skin test reactivity - perform TST on the day of vaccination or defer for 4-6 weeks

common: Varicella-like rash, localized or generalized and usually mild
Headache (more notable with ZOSTAVAX in older adults)
serious: Disseminated vaccine-strain varicella or zoster in immunocompromised recipients
rare: Herpes zoster from the vaccine strain (much less common and milder than wild-type)
Keratitis or other ocular complications (reported with zoster vaccination)
Encephalitis, ataxia, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (very rare, causal relationship not established)
emergency: Disseminated varicella-zoster infection in an immunocompromised host

monitoring: Observe for immediate allergic reactions after administration (have epinephrine available)
Monitor for vaccine-related rash within 1-3 weeks after vaccination
Advise avoidance of contact with high-risk susceptible persons (pregnant women, immunocompromised, neonates) if a rash develops
Confirm completion of the two-dose series for varicella prevention
counsel: This vaccine helps prevent chickenpox (VARIVAX) or shingles (ZOSTAVAX); two doses are needed for full varicella protection
Mild fever or a few chickenpox-like spots may appear in the weeks after vaccination
Children should avoid aspirin/salicylates for 6 weeks after varicella vaccination
Avoid becoming pregnant for at least 1 month (up to 3 months) after vaccination
Do not use antiviral herpes medicines (acyclovir, valacyclovir, famciclovir) around the time of vaccination unless advised
If a rash develops, avoid close contact with pregnant women, newborns, and people with weakened immune systems
Note: the live zoster vaccine (ZOSTAVAX) is no longer available in the US and has been replaced by the non-live recombinant shingles vaccine
pk: Immune response develops over several weeks after vaccination
Peak seroconversion within weeks of vaccination (after the second dose for VARIVAX)
Not applicable (vaccine - induces durable immune memory rather than measurable drug levels)
Long-term protection (years to decades for varicella); zoster vaccine efficacy wanes over several years
Store the lyophilized vaccine frozen per product labeling; protect from light; reconstitute with supplied diluent and use promptly (within 30 minutes)
pearls: Live attenuated Oka/Merck strain - contraindicated in pregnancy and significant immunosuppression for the whole class
VARIVAX (lower titer, varicella) and ZOSTAVAX (higher titer, zoster) share the same strain but differ in dose, schedule, and indication
ZOSTAVAX was discontinued in the US in 2020 and replaced by the non-live recombinant zoster vaccine (Shingrix)
Avoid antivirals active against herpesviruses around vaccination - they can inactivate the live vaccine virus
Avoid salicylates for 6 weeks after varicella vaccination (theoretical Reye syndrome risk)
Biologic vaccine - sourced from FDA package inserts (CBER) and ACIP recommendations rather than openFDA drug labels
missed: For the varicella 2-dose series, if the second dose is delayed give it as soon as feasible; the series does not need to be restarted. Follow the recommended minimum interval between doses. The live zoster vaccine was a single dose and is no longer marketed in the US.
overdose: Overdose is not clinically relevant for these vaccines; inadvertent administration of more than the recommended volume is managed with observation. Manage any hypersensitivity reaction supportively with epinephrine and standard anaphylaxis care.
